Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 111, verse 1–5 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His mention and sanctified be His names: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. (1) His wealth and what he earned will not avail him. (2) He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame. (3) And his wife, the carrier of firewood, (4) around her neck a rope of palm fiber.﴾ (5)

He, may His mention be exalted, says: "Lost are the hands of Abu Lahab, and lost is he." What is meant by His saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ is that his deeds have perished. Some of the people of Arabic grammar used to say: His saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ is an invocation (du'a') against him from Allah.

As for His saying ﴿and perish he﴾, it is a statement of fact. It is related that in the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it reads: "Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and he has indeed perished." The presence of "qad" (indeed) in it indicates that it is a statement of fact, and this is illustrated by the saying of one speaker to another: "May Allah destroy you, and you have indeed been destroyed; may He make you righteous, and you have indeed been made so."

In agreement with what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾: that is, they have been lost, and he has perished.
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding Allah's saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾: "At-tabb" is the loss. He said: Abu Lahab said to the Prophet ﷺ: "What will be given to me if I believe in you?" He said: "As the Muslims are given." He said: "Do I have no advantage over them?" He said: "And what do you seek?" He said: "Ruin to this religion, ruin! That I and these should be equal!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾, meaning: by what their hands have done.
- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatadah: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾, he said: the hands of Abu Lahab have been lost, and he has been lost.

It has been said that this surah was revealed concerning Abu Lahab, because when the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to give the call specifically to his kinsmen, when there was revealed to him: ﴿And warn your nearest kinsmen﴾, and he gathered them for the call, Abu Lahab said to him: "Ruin to you all day! Is it for this that you summoned us?"

Mention of the reports transmitted concerning this:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ climbed al-Safa and called out: "Ya sabahah!" Quraysh gathered to him and said: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Tell me, if I were to inform you that an enemy is about to attack you at morning or evening, would you not believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Ruin to you! Is it for this that you summoned us and gathered us?!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ to its end.
- Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When there was revealed ﴿And warn your nearest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood upon al-Safa and then called out: "Ya sabahah!" The people gathered to him, some coming in person and others sending their messengers. He said: "O Banu Hashim, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Fihr, O Banu ... Tell me, if I were to inform you that horsemen were at the foot of this mountain" — he meant that they would raid you — "would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Ruin to you all day! Is it for this that you summoned us?" Then there was revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And warn your nearest kinsmen, and your people among them, the sincere ones﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he climbed al-Safa and cried out: "Ya sabahah!" They said: "Who is this calling out?" They said: "Muhammad." So they gathered to him, and he said: "O Banu Fulan, O Banu Fulan, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, O Banu Abd Manaf!" They gathered to him, and he said: "Tell me, if I were to inform you that horsemen were coming out at the foot of this mountain, would you believe me?" They said: "We have not tested you as a liar." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Ruin to you! Did you gather us only for this?" Then he stood, and this surah was revealed: "Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and he has indeed perished," thus Al-A'mash recited it to the end of the surah.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding His saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾: when the Prophet ﷺ sent for him and for others, and he mentioned them, Abu Lahab said: "Ruin to you! For this did you send for us?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾. Abu Lahab was the paternal uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, and his name was Abd al-Uzza.

* *

His saying: ﴿His wealth and what he earned will not avail him﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: What availed him his wealth, and what he warded off of the wrath of Allah upon him, ﴿and what he earned﴾, and they are his children. In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said this:

- Al-Hasan ibn Dawud ibn Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Mu'ammar, from Ibn Khaytham, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: The sons of Abu Lahab came to Ibn Abbas and began to dispute about the house. Ibn Abbas stood and separated them, though his sight had been lost, and one of them pushed him until he fell upon the bedding. He became angry and said: "Remove from me the wretched earnings!"
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Muhammad ibn Sufyan, from a man of Banu Makhzum, from Ibn Abbas, that he once saw the sons of Abu Lahab fighting, and he began to separate them and said: "These are of what he earned."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿What he earned﴾, he said: his children.
- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding Allah's saying ﴿and what he earned﴾, he said: his children are of his earnings.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding Allah's saying ﴿and what he earned﴾, he said: his children.

* *

His saying: ﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame﴾

He says: Abu Lahab will burn in a fire of blazing flame.

* *

His saying: ﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾

He says: Abu Lahab will burn, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, in a fire of blazing flame. The readers differed regarding the reading of ﴿the carrier of firewood﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah, Kufah and Basrah read it as "ḥammālatu al-ḥaṭabi" in the nominative (raf'), except Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq, who read it in the accusative (nasb), as has been related from him.

It is related from ʿĀṣim with differing reports, with both the nominative and the accusative transmitted from him. Whoever read it in the nominative made it an attribute (na't) of the wife, and made the nominative for the wife the preceding statement, namely "will burn". It is also permissible that its nominative be the attribute, which is His saying ﴿around her neck﴾, and "ḥammālah" be an attribute of the wife. As for the accusative, it is by way of censure (dhamm), and it may also be that its accusative is by way of detachment (qaṭʿ) from the wife, since the wife is definite and "carrier of firewood" is indefinite.

[[The poem is from the Diwan (p. 131) and the Naqa'id (p. 773), and it appears in the explanation of the verse of Surah al-Shu'ara (26:4). It satirises Jarir and his people, Banu Kulayb ibn Yarbu'. Al-arbaq: plural of ribq, a rope with which young sheep are tied so they do not nurse. Taqallada al-sayf: he placed its hilt on his shoulder. Al-kumah, plural of kammi: a champion of great valour. It describes Banu Kulayb as lowly, miserly shepherds whose only concern is the herding of sheep, while warriors endure the heat of battle for long days until the iron of their coats of mail rusts on their bodies from sweat.]]

The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is the nominative, because it is the more eloquent of the two and because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿the carrier of firewood﴾. Some of them said: She used to bring thorns and throw them on the path of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that they would enter his foot when he went out to prayer.

Mention of those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾, he said: She used to carry thorns and throw them on the way of the Prophet ﷺ, so as to wound him and his companions. And it is said: "the carrier of firewood" means: a carrier of tales.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from a man of Hamdan called Yazid ibn Zayd, that the wife of Abu Lahab used to throw thorns on the path of the Prophet ﷺ, so there was revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab ... and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾.
- Abu Hurayrah al-Dab'i, Muhammad ibn Firas, narrated to me, saying: Abu Amir narrated to us, from Qurrah ibn Khalid, from Atiyyah al-Jadali, regarding His saying ﴿the carrier of firewood﴾, he said: She used to place thorny shrubs on the path of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that he would tread upon it as upon a sand dune.
- It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾: She used to carry thorns and throw them on the path of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ to wound him.
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾: She used to bring branches of thorns and throw them at night on the path of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Others said: She was called "carrier of firewood" because she used to gather tales like firewood, walk about with slander, and reproach the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for his poverty.

Mention of those who said this:

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mu'tamir said: Muhammad claims that Ikrimah said: "the carrier of firewood": she used to walk about with slander.
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾, he said: She used to walk about with slander.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the carrier of firewood﴾, he said: the slander.
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾: that is, she used to transmit reports from some people to others.
- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾, he said: She used to gather speech like firewood and walk about with slander.

Some of them said: She used to reproach the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for poverty, and she used to gather firewood, so she was reproached for gathering firewood.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾, he said: She used to walk about with slander.

The most preferred of the two opinions in this matter, in my judgement as to what is correct, is the view of the one who said: She used to carry thorns and throw them on the path of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, because that is the more evident meaning of it.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Isa ibn Yazid, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Zayd, who was the closest of people to Masruq, who said: When there was revealed ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾, news reached the wife of Abu Lahab that the Prophet ﷺ was satirising her. She said: "Why does he satirise me? Have you seen me as Muhammad says, carrying firewood, ﴿around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾?" She remained for a time, then came to him and said: "Your Lord has forsaken you and abandoned you." So Allah revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still; your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

* *

His saying ﴿around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾

He says: around her neck. The Arabs call the neck "jid" (جيد), and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"Your eyes are her eyes, and your colour is her colour, and your neck is hers, except that it is not bare."

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said this:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding Allah's saying ﴿around her neck a rope﴾: on her neck.

* *

His saying: ﴿a rope of palm fiber﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding this. Some of them said: They are ropes that are made in Makkah.

Mention of those who said this:

- It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾: a rope of tree-fibre, which is the rope with which she used to gather firewood.
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿a rope of palm fiber﴾, he said: They are ropes that are made in Makkah. It is also said: "al-masad" is the staff that is in the pulley, and it is also said: "al-masad" is a necklace of cowrie shells.
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿a rope of palm fiber﴾: ropes of tree-fibre that grow in Yemen, having masad, which were twisted. And He said ﴿a rope of palm fiber﴾: a rope of fire around her neck.

Others said: al-masad is fibre (al-layf).

Mention of those who said this:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Yazid, from Urwah, regarding ﴿around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾: a chain of iron, its length seventy cubits.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from a man called Yazid, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding ﴿around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾: a chain whose length is seventy cubits.
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Yazid, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding ﴿around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾: a chain whose length is seventy cubits.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from his father, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿of palm fiber﴾: of iron.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾: a rope around her neck in the Fire, like a collar, its length seventy cubits.

Others said: al-masad is the iron that is in the pulley.

Mention of those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾: the iron piece that is in the pulley.
- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿a rope of palm fiber﴾: the wooden part of the pulley is of iron.
- al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿a rope of palm fiber﴾: the iron piece of the pulley.
- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatadah, and he said: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mu'tamir said: Muhammad claims that Ikrimah said: "around her neck a rope of palm fiber": it is the iron that is in the middle of the pulley.

Others said: It is a necklace of cowrie shells around her neck.

Mention of those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾: a necklace of cowrie shells.
- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿a rope of palm fiber﴾: a necklace of cowrie shells.

The most preferred of the sayings in this matter, in my judgement as to what is correct, is the view of the one who said: It is a rope composed of various kinds of materials, and for this reason the people of interpretation differed in its explanation in the manner we have mentioned. Among what confirms the soundness of what we have said in this matter is the saying of the rajiz (rhymed verse reciter):

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 111, verses 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

*And a rope (masad) twisted from camels, tawny, noble, rich in marrow, fine-boned,*

[[By his saying "the temporary definiteness" (al-ma'rifa al-mu'aqqata), he means definiteness in the sense of a proper name, which specifies its referent absolutely and without qualification. So your saying "Zayd" specifies absolutely, or definitely. The noun defined by "al" (the definite article) specifies its referent only as long as the "al" is attached to it; when it is detached, the specification is lost. See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:7.]]

Then he made its twisting from various things. Likewise, the masad that is around the neck of Abu Lahab's wife was twisted from various things: from palm fibre, from iron and from bark. He placed around her neck a collar like a necklace of cowrie shells (wadi'). Among the poetry on this is the saying of al-A'sha:

*In the evening it turns its door's bolt away from us,*
*a lock creaking like the groaning of the mountains (amsad)*

[[The phrase in context: "whether... the people were described... or were not described," and between these two there is a long section, in keeping with Abu Ja'far's method in his exposition.]]

He means by al-amsad: the plural of masad, which means mountains.

End of the tafsir of Surah Tabbat.

His saying: ﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾

He says: Abu Lahab will burn, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, in a fire of blazing flame. The readers differed regarding the reading of ﴿the carrier of firewood﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah, Kufah and Basrah read it as "ḥammālatu al-ḥaṭabi" in the nominative (raf'), except Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq, who read it in the accusative (nasb), as has been related from him.

It is related from ʿĀṣim with differing reports, with both the nominative and the accusative transmitted from him. Whoever read it in the nominative made it an attribute (na't) of the wife, and made the nominative for the wife the preceding statement, namely "will burn". It is also permissible that its nominative be the attribute, which is His saying ﴿around her neck﴾, and "ḥammālah" be an attribute of the wife. As for the accusative, it is by way of censure (dhamm), and it may also be that its accusative is by way of detachment (qaṭʿ) from the wife, since the wife is definite and "carrier of firewood" is indefinite.

[[The poem is from the Diwan (p. 131) and the Naqa'id (p. 773), and it appears in the explanation of the verse of Surah al-Shu'ara (26:4). It satirises Jarir and his people, Banu Kulayb ibn Yarbu'. He, may His mention be exalted, says: "Lost are the hands of Abu Lahab, and lost is he." What is meant by His saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ is that his deeds have perished. Some of the people of Arabic grammar used to say: His saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ is an invocation (du'a') against him from Allah.

As for His saying ﴿and perish he﴾, it is a statement of fact. It is related that in the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it reads: "Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and he has indeed perished." The presence of "qad" (indeed) in it indicates that it is a statement of fact, and this is illustrated by the saying of one speaker to another: "May Allah destroy you, and you have indeed been destroyed; may He make you righteous, and you have indeed been made so."

In agreement with what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

His saying: ﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾

He says: Abu Lahab will burn, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, in a fire of blazing flame. The readers differed regarding the reading of ﴿the carrier of firewood﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah, Kufah and Basrah read it as "ḥammālatu al-ḥaṭabi" in the nominative (raf'), except Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq, who read it in the accusative (nasb), as has been related from him.

It is related from ʿĀṣim with differing reports, with both the nominative and the accusative transmitted from him. Whoever read it in the nominative made it an attribute (na't) of the wife, and made the nominative for the wife the preceding statement, namely "will burn". It is also permissible that its nominative be the attribute, which is His saying ﴿around her neck﴾, and "ḥammālah" be an attribute of the wife. As for the accusative, it is by way of censure (dhamm), and it may also be that its accusative is by way of detachment (qaṭʿ) from the wife, since the wife is definite and "carrier of firewood" is indefinite.

[[The poem is from the Diwan (p. 131) and the Naqa'id (p. 773), and it appears in the explanation of the verse of Surah al-Shu'ara (26:4). It satirises Jarir and his people, Banu Kulayb ibn Yarbu'. Al-arbaq: plural of ribq, a rope with which young sheep are tied so they do not nurse. Taqallada al-sayf: he placed its hilt on his shoulder. Al-kumah, plural of kammi: a champion of great valour. It describes Banu Kulayb as lowly, miserly shepherds whose only concern is the herding of sheep, while warriors endure the heat of battle for long days until the iron of their coats of mail rusts on their bodies from sweat.]]

The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is the nominative, because it is the more eloquent of the two and because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.
